objectives.text: Given the type of a transformer, DESCRIBE the operating characteristics and applications for that transformer type.

enabling.text: DEFINE the following terms as they pertain to transformers:
DESCRIBE the differences between a wye-connected and delta-connected transformer.
Given the type of connection and turns ratios for the primary and secondary of a transformer, CALCULATE voltage, current, and power for each of the following types:
STATE the applications of each of the following types of transformers:

passages.quote: The inducing of an EMF in a coil by magnetic flux lines generated in another coil is called mutual induction.
The turns ratio is defined as the ratio of turns of wire in the primary winding to the number of turns of wire in the secondary winding.
The ratio between the two impedances is referred to as the impedance ratio
Maximum power is transferred from one circuit to another through a transformer when the impedances are equal, or matched.
Efficiency of a transformer is the ratio of the power output to the power input
The coil of a transformer that is energized from an AC source is called the primary winding (coil), and the coil that delivers this AC to the load is called the secondary winding (coil)
The voltage of the windings in a transformer is directly proportional to the number of turns on the coils.
the voltage ratio is equal to the turns ratio.
the transformer is referred to as a "step-up" transformer.
The current in the windings of a transformer is inversely proportional to the voltage in the windings.
In the delta connection, all three phases are connected in series to form a closed loop
In the wye connection, three common ends of each phase are connected together at a common terminal
Distribution transformers are generally used in electrical power distribution and transmission systems.
Power transformers are used in electronic circuits and come in many different types and applications.
Control transformers are generally used in electronic circuits that require constant voltage or constant current with a low power or volt-amp rating.
The auto transformer is generally used in low power applications where a variable voltage is required.
Isolation transformers are normally low power transformers used to isolate noise from or to ground electronic circuits.
The instrument potential transformer (PT) steps down voltage of a circuit to a low value that can be effectively and safely used for operation of instruments
secondary line current = 4(20) = 80 amps
A current transformer should always be short-circuited when not connected to an external load.

body.text: Turns ratio = NP / NS
The impedance ratio equals the square of the turns ratio, so a set turns ratio can match impedances.
Efficiency = (Power output / Power input) x 100
Energy is transferred by magnetic induction from one set of coils to another by means of a varying magnetic flux.

body.alt: Core-type transformer with primary and secondary coils on separate legs of an iron core, connected to an AC source and a load.

body.text: VP / VS = NP / NS
If the secondary voltage is greater than the primary voltage, the transformer is a step-up transformer. If it is less, it is a step-down transformer.
IS / IP = NP / NS
A transformer that steps up voltage steps down the current proportionally.
All transformers have copper and core losses. Copper loss is power lost to the ohmic resistance of the windings.
Core losses are caused by hysteresis and eddy current losses.

o: The inducing of an EMF in a coil by magnetic flux lines generated in another coil
The ratio of primary to secondary turns
The loss of power in the windings
The opposition to current in a coil
checks.x: The inducing of an EMF in a coil by magnetic flux lines generated in another coil is called mutual induction.

checks.q: A transformer has 1200 primary turns and 300 secondary turns, with 480 volts on the primary. What is the secondary voltage?
checks.x: The voltage ratio equals the turns ratio: VS = 480 x 300/1200 = 120 volts.

checks.q: When are impedances matched across a transformer most useful?
o: To transfer maximum power from one circuit to another
checks.x: Maximum power is transferred from one circuit to another through a transformer when the impedances are equal, or matched.

checks.q: A transformer takes in 5000 watts and delivers 4500 watts. What is its efficiency?

body.text: Three-phase transformer operation is identical to single-phase, except that three single-phase windings are used.

body.alt: Delta connection: three windings in a closed triangle with lines from the corners.
Wye connection: three windings joined at a neutral point N, with the other ends going to the line.

body.text: The windings may be connected to form a three-phase bank in four ways: ∆-∆, ∆-Y, Y-∆, and Y-Y.

body.alt: Four transformer bank connections, delta-delta, delta-wye, wye-delta, and wye-wye, marked with voltages and currents.

body.text: With line voltage V and line current I, a delta primary winding has voltage V, and a wye primary winding has voltage V divided by √3.
A delta primary winding has phase current I divided by √3, and a wye primary winding has phase current I.
With turns ratio a, the secondary line current is aI for ∆-∆ and Y-Y, and √3 aI for Y-∆.

checks.q: How are the three phases of a delta connection arranged?
o: In series to form a closed loop
All in parallel with the load
Each to a separate core only
checks.x: In the delta connection, all three phases are connected in series to form a closed loop.

checks.q: Line voltage to a Y-Y transformer bank is 173 volts. Using √3 = 1.73, what is the voltage across each primary winding?
checks.x: In a wye primary, winding voltage is line voltage divided by √3: 173 / 1.73 = 100 volts.

checks.q: A ∆-∆ bank has a turns ratio of 5:1 and a primary line current of 10 amps. What is the secondary line current?
checks.x: For ∆-∆, secondary line current is aI = 5 x 10 = 50 amps. In the handbook's example, a 4:1 ratio and 20 amps give 80 amps.

body.text: This class has the highest power ratings and the highest continuous voltage rating.
The auto transformer consists of only one winding. Tapping it at certain points gives different voltages.

body.alt: Auto transformer schematic: one winding with an input across it and an output tap.

body.text: A transformer cannot pass DC voltage from primary to secondary, so DC such as noise is isolated.
The instrument current transformer (CT) steps down the current of a circuit to a lower value and is used in the same types of equipment.
Otherwise the magnetizing current builds up a large flux, inducing an excessively high voltage in the secondary under no load.

checks.q: Which transformer type has the highest power and voltage ratings?
checks.x: Distribution transformers have the highest power, or volt-ampere, ratings and the highest continuous voltage rating.

checks.q: Which transformer has only one winding and gives a variable voltage?
checks.x: The auto transformer consists of only one winding, generally used in low power applications where a variable voltage is required.

checks.q: What should be done with a current transformer that is not connected to an external load?
checks.x: A current transformer should always be short-circuited when not connected to an external load.

checks.q: What is an isolation transformer used for?
o: To isolate noise from or to ground electronic circuits
checks.x: Isolation transformers are normally low power transformers used to isolate noise from or to ground electronic circuits.

checks.q: What does an instrument potential transformer do?
checks.x: The instrument potential transformer steps down voltage of a circuit to a low value that can be used for operation of instruments.

checks.q: Where are control transformers generally used?
o: Circuits needing constant voltage or current at low power
checks.x: Control transformers are generally used in electronic circuits that require constant voltage or constant current with a low power or volt-amp rating.

examples.problem: A transformer has a primary voltage of 240 volts, 250 turns in the primary, and 50 turns in the secondary. Find the secondary voltage.

examples.title: Primary winding voltage
examples.problem: Line voltage is 440 V to a three-phase transformer bank. Find the voltage across each primary winding.
steps: Y-Y and Y-∆: primary voltage = V / √3.
examples.answer: 440 volts for a delta primary and 254.3 volts for a wye primary

examples.title: Secondary line current
examples.problem: Primary line current is 20 amps and the turns ratio is 4:1. Find the secondary line current for Y-∆.

facts.a: One whose secondary voltage is greater than its primary voltage.

facts.q: How do transformer current and voltage relate?
facts.a: The current in the windings is inversely proportional to the voltage in the windings.

facts.q: What is the voltage ratio of a transformer equal to?
What is the primary winding of a transformer?
facts.a: The coil that is energized from an AC source.
In electronic circuits, in many different types and applications.

summary.text: The turns ratio is the ratio of turns of wire in the primary winding to the number of turns in the secondary winding.
In a delta connection, all three phases are connected in series to form a closed loop. In a wye connection, three common ends of each phase are connected together at a common terminal.
Distribution transformers are generally used in power distribution and transmission systems.
Instrument potential and current transformers are used for operation of instruments and protective relays.
